newsitem.title: USA: Techs resists Dow selloff, Nasdaq hits 5th record.
newsitem.headline: Techs resists Dow selloff, Nasdaq hits 5th record.

text.p: Nasdaq shares hit a fifth consecutive record high Wednesday as technology stocks resisted a broad selloff that pulled the Dow Jones Industrial Average down 120 points, traders said.

The Nasdaq composite index gained 1.50 points or 0.10 percent to close unofficially at 1486.60, which tops the previous record closing high set Tuesday. The session was mixed with declining issues beating gaining issues 2,410 to 1,994 on heavy volume of 712 million shares.
"Internet stocks were the strongest, but the techs were good overall. They seemed to ignore what was happening in the rest of the market," one trader said.
Traders said investors appeared to taking profits in Blue Chip stocks and moving towards technology issues, which had been battered in the weeks before the most recent rally.
Computer networking company 3Com Corp, the most active Nasdaq issue, gained 2-9/16 to 52-5/8 after Merrill Lynch upgraded the stock.
DSC Communications Corp added 3-15/16 to 26-1/16 after UBS Securities upgraded the stock and raised earnings estimates. Both Cisco Systems Inc and Dell Computer Corp hit new 52-week highs.
